headline_drivers: FQ4 (Mar-2026) earnings on 2026-05-18: EPS of ~$0.52 beat consensus ~$0.49; continued strong profitability with TTM EPS $2.28 and FY earnings expected to grow ~38% next year (MarketBeat, earnings release/8-K).

Valuation re-rating after print: stock still trades at ~16.5x TTM EPS vs ~31x sector and ~39x broader market P/E, with P/B ~2.6x, prompting investors to rotate into a profitable, under-valued ad/marketing data infrastructure name.

Improved growth/profitability narrative: Street now models ~37–38% EPS growth next year (from ~$2.07 to ~$2.85), suggesting a margin and earnings inflection in a business-services/marketing-tech name many investors had written off as ex-growth.

Momentum/technical follow-through after the 05-18 volume spike: the stock appears on top-5d and volspike_gapper screens, RSI in the 95th percentile, with the last few sessions driven more by trend/momentum funds than new incremental news.
summary: The move in LiveRamp over the past few weeks is primarily a fundamental re-rating off the May 18 earnings print, where the company delivered another clean beat (EPS ~$0.52 vs ~$0.49) and reinforced a story of accelerating earnings power, with Street models now calling for nearly 38% EPS growth next year. Against that backdrop, the stock still screens as inexpensive at ~16.5x TTM earnings and ~2.6x book versus richer marketing-tech and business-services comps, which has pulled in fundamental buyers rotating into profitable, cash-generating data infrastructure names. Once that re-rating started, a big volume spike on the day of earnings pushed RAMP onto momentum and gap-up screens; since then, much of the additional upside over the last 5–10 sessions looks like technical/momentum follow-through rather than a new discrete catalyst. I did not find evidence of a specific named mega-cap customer deal, regulatory event, or M&A announcement driving the move; the reaction is mainly to stronger-than-expected earnings, improved forward EPS trajectory, and subsequent momentum buying.
